name: Zulu Kingdom
summary: A Southern African kingdom built by Shaka from about 1816 through military reform. It defeated a British army at Isandlwana in 1879 before Britain broke it up.

terrain.value: Rolling grassland, river valleys and hills between the Drakensberg and the Indian Ocean.

disasters.value: A severe drought around the 1800s is linked to the conflicts that formed the kingdom.

urbanisation.value: Large royal homesteads (amakhanda) served as capitals and barracks.

migration.value: Wars of the period (the “Mfecane”, a debated concept) displaced many peoples.

economicBase.value: Cattle herding and farming of sorghum and maize.

tradeRoutes.value: Trade with Portuguese at Delagoa Bay and British traders at Port Natal.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: Wealth was counted in cattle; captured cattle went to the king.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Zulu Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Laband, Rope of Sand (1995)

inequality.value: The royal house and chiefs controlled cattle and the labour of the regiments.

governmentType.value: Absolute monarchy, with the king commanding the age-regiments.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Zulu Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Laband, Rope of Sand (1995)

succession.value: Often violent: Shaka was killed by his half-brothers in 1828.

institutions.value: Age-grade regiments (amabutho) that served the king and could not marry without permission.

stability.value: Civil wars between royal brothers (1840, 1856) and after Britain split the kingdom (1883–84).

eliteConflict.value: Rival royal brothers and chiefs; the British divided the kingdom among chiefs after 1879.

armyAndTech.value: Standing regiments with the short stabbing spear (iklwa), large cowhide shields and the “bull’s horns” encircling tactic.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Zulu Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Laband, Rope of Sand (1995)

majorWars.value: Battle of Blood River (1838); Anglo-Zulu War (1879): Isandlwana (Zulu victory) and Ulundi (British victory).

territoryChange.value: About 207,000 km² in 1822, shrinking after wars with the Voortrekkers and Britain.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Zulu Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Laband, Rope of Sand (1995)

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: the Ndwandwe, the Voortrekkers and Britain.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Zulu Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Laband, Rope of Sand (1995)

inventions.value: Military reforms rather than new technology.

scienceEducation.value: Knowledge was kept by oral tradition and praise poetry (izibongo).

openness.value: Traded with Europeans but resisted settlement.

religion.value: Zulu religion centred on ancestors, later with Christian missions.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Zulu Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Laband, Rope of Sand (1995)

languageWriting.value: isiZulu; written in Latin script by missionaries.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Zulu Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Laband, Rope of Sand (1995)

artsArchitecture.value: Beadwork with coded colours and beehive-shaped homes.

sharedIdentity.value: Loyalty to the king and a growing Zulu identity.

neighbours.value: The Ndwandwe, Swazi, Voortrekkers and British Natal.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Zulu Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Laband, Rope of Sand (1995)

riseSignals.value: Shaka’s military reforms and defeat of the Ndwandwe (1818–1820).
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Zulu Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Laband, Rope of Sand (1995)

declineSignals.value: Defeat at Ulundi (1879) and the British division of the kingdom.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Zulu Kingdom (checked 6 Nov 2026); Laband, Rope of Sand (1995)

outcome.value: Absorbed into Natal; a Zulu king still reigns today.

sources.value: Oral history, missionary and British records. Checked against Wikipedia (“Zulu Kingdom”).

overallCertainty.value: Medium. Shaka’s reign is heavily mythologised.

knownFor.label: Iklwa stabbing spear
knownFor.note: A short spear for close fighting.

knownFor.label: Isandlwana
knownFor.note: A major victory over a British army.
